node_definition.done_when: On 2026-10-02 at about 15:01, `reckon crew gc --repo ~/Code/reckon --project reckon --apply` exited with 'Error: worktree .../s25-picker/review-of-picker-prototype is unavailable: tree is no longer available' and reclaimed nothing. One registered worktree, whose directory is gone while git still lists it, aborted the whole collection. The dry run (without --apply) classified every tree and did not raise. The raise is reckon/crew/routing.py _inspect_workspace (`raise CrewError(f"worktree {path} is unavailable: ...")`) on the apply path. The node makes gc --apply treat an unavailable worktree as the dry run does: report it in the payload with its detail, leave it untouched (no prune of another session's registration), and carry on reclaiming every reclaimable tree. Any caller that relies on the raise outside gc keeps its behaviour, or the node names each caller it changes. tests/test_gc_applies_past_a_vanished_worktree.py builds, in a temporary repository, one reclaimable integrated worktree and one registered worktree whose directory was removed. It asserts that gc --apply reclaims the first, reports the second as unavailable, and leaves the second's git registration in place. The declared negative control is executed and logged. Base and head arms of every test file that calls gc or _inspect_workspace (found by grep at the base) show zero added failures, each log ending in its pytest summary and EXIT= line, run with -n 8.
node_definition.goal: crew gc --apply reports a vanished worktree and still reclaims the rest
